changes: [[Set]] fast path: an own writable data property of an entirely ordinary receiver (no internal-method overrides, no arguments alias for the key) is stored directly; arrays (exotic define), typed arrays, proxies, mapped arguments and other receivers keep OrdinarySet.
Reference-based global reads (compound assignment, update) use one prototype-chain walk on an all-ordinary chain; exotic chains keep HasProperty, HasProperty, Get.
Constant-key member references skip objectPropertyKey (ToPropertyKey of a string is the string; the adjacent get/set helper repeats RequireObjectCoercible at the same point).

Property reads lower to readObjectValueProperty (constant or retained key) and readObjectValuePropertyKey (plain computed key: RequireObjectCoercible, ToPropertyKey, Get in order), which return the value and throw in the realm instead of {error,value} records; both share propertyValueOf with getObjectValuePropertyWithReceiver, so J's primitive reads through the realm prototype apply to every read path.
